scope: Primary-source exterior reference audit for Baker House, Simmons Hall, and Maseeh Hall. Reference research only; no model/public files changed.
method: Downloaded public image URLs exposed by official owner, architect, or foundation pages and visually inspected them. Geometry recommendations are visual interpretations unless a written source is identified. Local details can be estimated to preserve recognizable form.

baker.orientation: Smooth serpentine residential facade faces south/Charles River and Memorial Drive. Angular stair/common-space facade faces north/athletic fields and Amherst Alley.
criticalShape: Use the actual long serpentine room strip, not a straight slab with a wavy applied skin. Ends include substantial near-blind brick planes.
Low dining/Moon Garden pavilion projects toward the river from the central part of the slab; it has strong horizontal roof edges and ribbon glazing, unlike the dorm-room window rhythm.

North facade is strongly different: two terracotta-colored suspended stair wings form an approximate V when viewed from the athletic fields. Stair flights and short landing breaks define their lower edge; window groups step with the stairs. A recessed central linking wall has stacked horizontal window bands.
North western section (image right in baker-home.jpg) retains darker brick and irregular small windows. Do not cover the whole north facade in terracotta panels.
Flat roof has low light-colored service volumes and open pergola-like elements; no pitched roof.
baker.windows: South facade: six room-floor window rows following the wave, generally rectangular windows with larger upper glazing and a smaller lower sash strip. North: irregular groups and ribbon-like runs; never mirror the south grid.
baker.materials: Dark textured reddish-brown brick; warmer smooth terracotta/pink-red stair faces; pale concrete plinth/edges; light window frames; muted gray entrance canopy.

entrance.confidence: high for side and architectural relation; no surveyed point claimed
entrance.location: North-side recessed courtyard at the bottom between the two sloping stair wings.
entrance.appearance: Short wide dark gray flat canopy, narrow supports, recessed brown timber double doors, and a short flight of approach steps. The official Guide photograph explicitly captions this as the front entrance.
entrance.limitation: The source model's approximately 17x16 m northern low appendage is not formally identified by these references. Do not equate its entire area to the small visible canopy.

pitfalls: Do not place the main door in the south dining pavilion by default.
Do not model the suspended stairs as two conventional rectangular stair towers.
baker-foundation-1949.jpg is a historical plan drawing, not a photograph.

simmons.orientation: Main long photographed elevation faces Vassar Street/Briggs athletic fields. Architect's color elevation identifies it as south elevation. The main entrance plan has north up and the entrance at the east end near its south corner.
criticalShape: Three high ten-story portions with two unequal lowered terrace roof lines; use the visibly unequal spans and terrace heights rather than three identical towers.

Five large-scale mass openings include terraces, corner recesses and lower openings. Some have a recessed colored/perforated backing wall and a few larger windows; they are not all completely through-cut voids.
Several large irregular atrium windows have sloping sides and rounded/curved lower corners, distinct from the rectilinear major recesses.
Street level includes long glazed/awning zones. The middle-right large exterior stair opening is separate from the main east-end door.
The short ends and return faces also carry the fine grid, with local larger recesses and solid/infilled cells.

windows.longFacadeGrid: 116 columns by 31 rows, explicitly stated by MIT's 2022 projection-installation report.
windows.roomRhythm: Nine little square operable windows per single room, normally three by three; approximately three small-window rows per story, not one.
windows.gridPitch: 40 inches (1.016 m), stated by structural engineer Guy Nordenson.
windows.detail: Deeply recessed glazing; silver-gray flat aluminum outer grid; colored jambs and heads inside the openings; narrow dark projecting sill edge. Some cells are deliberately filled for structural stress.
windows.color: Predominantly red/orange/yellow concentrations with selected blue/green cells; do not randomly color outer aluminum grid bars.

dimensions.structuralEngineer: SGH's primary project description gives 385 ft long, 100 ft high, 54 ft wide (approximately 117.35 x 30.48 x 16.46 m).
dimensions.discrepancy: Steven Holl project narrative says 330 ft long. Prefer surveyed model envelope plus actual photo proportions; 116 x 40 in = 386.67 ft independently supports the longer grid envelope.
dimensions.access: SGH dimension text was accessible in web search extract; direct page returned 403. No restriction bypass was attempted.

entrance.confidence: high for relative location in the official public plan, document dated 2013
entrance.location: East end of the long building, near the southeast corner, opening onto the east-facing short wall in a small setback.
entrance.evidence: Official floor-1 plan labels the rightmost lower end entrance as 1=Main Entrance. The prominent middle-right external stair is floor-2 egress, not the main ground-level entry.

pitfalls: Do not reduce the facade to ten tall window rows.
Do not treat all five large openings as empty tunnels.
Do not use the watercolor section as as-built exterior evidence.
Do not transpose the large stair opening and the main east-end door.

maseeh.orientation: W1 at Massachusetts Avenue/Memorial Drive. River-facing front is south; the separately photographed Amherst Street entrance is north/campus side.
criticalShape: South elevation has two projecting wing ends framing a recessed central courtyard, not one flat plane.
Each south wing has an inner faceted/octagonal tower capped by a dark ribbed copper cupola and an outer square crenellated corner. Preserve the separation and roof silhouette.
Faceted projecting window bays and limestone quoins articulate the vertical masonry. Stone horizontal bands interrupt the tall brick faces.
North entrance is crowned by a central stepped/curved ornamental brick gable with pale stone trim and finials.
River courtyard retains a separate recessed vestibule/canopy. Do not copy the north central gable directly onto the outer south wing fronts.
maseeh.windows: Mostly vertically proportioned white/light sash windows, some paired in stone surrounds. Preserve facade bay differences, prominent stone surrounds/bands, and projecting bay corners rather than a uniform window lattice.
maseeh.materials: Textured red-brown brick, warm pale limestone trim/quoins, light sashes. Cupola caps are dark aged copper with visible ribs and thin greenish finials/weather vanes; they are not bright solid-green cones.

entrance.north: Amherst Street entry: approach steps, dark bowed glass/metal canopy, recessed glass/door zone, large central stone arch flanked by smaller arches beneath the tall ornamental gable.
entrance.south: Memorial Drive side: entrance set back within the courtyard between the two wings. Lower door detail is partly occluded by mature trees in the MIT full-front photograph.
entrance.sourceDistinction: Existing output/design/mit-20261021/references/maseeh-2011.jpg depicts Amherst Street, per the official caption; it is not the Memorial Drive front.
entrance.architectNotes: MDS renovation page distinguishes restored main entrance canopy and recreated courtyard vestibule canopy overlooking the river.

pitfalls: Do not make cupola drums cylindrical; the photos show faceted masonry.
Do not confuse current Ashdown NW35 with historic Ashdown/current Maseeh W1.
maseeh-river-overall.jpg is actually a roof/cupola close-up despite its filename.

limitations: References are retained for visual research; no general image-reuse license is inferred.
No claim of exact as-built window-by-window fidelity for unphotographed rear walls.
Simmons public entrance plan is dated 2013; use it for exterior architectural position, not current operational policies.
